recipes.name: Fried Onion Rings
ingredients_raw: 4 onions, peeled and sliced into rings

steps.text: In a large, deep skillet, heat oil to 365 degrees F (180 degrees C).
In a medium bowl, combine flour, beer, salt, and pepper. Mix until smooth. Dredge onion slices in the batter, until evenly coated. Deep fry in the hot oil until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.

raw_recipe.headline: Fried Onion Rings
raw_recipe.description: These are very delicate and the best I have had. My ex was a fanatic when it came to onion rings, and thought this recipe to be the best he ever had. I have also made other veggies in this batter. It can be refrigerated or frozen, then reheated in oven or microwave. Carbonated water can be substituted for beer in this recipe.
raw_recipe.name: Fried Onion Rings

review.reviewBody: This is almost identical to my favorite batter recipe. However, the idea of substituting carbonated water for beer is marvelous! No other batter recipe I have ever read, has made that substitution suggestion.

This is virtually the same recipe our family made since I was a kid, with one major difference: we start by soaking the onion rings in buttermilk first. It's best to soak them for about two minutes, but if you're in a hury, just dredge them through the buttermilk and then the batter. They ALWAYS get rave reviews!!
Great light batter. Season to taste with Old Bay. Best when batter sits covered countertop for minimum 1 hour. Keep warm in 200* oven. Cooked rings do freeze well - reheat gently in oven.

Delicious - although the batter is super messy! I added seasoned salt, garlic, pepper and a bit of sugar to the batter. Will most likely make again however will add more liquid as my batter was a tad too thick.

Great recipe. Very close to my own. I find if I use half AP flour and half corn starch, the onion rings stay crispy for a long time. One tip is do not drain on paper towel but, a cooling rack set over paper towels. I use this for shrimp and fish too. For seafood I sometimes add a lime flavored sparkling water and some Old Bay seasoning and a touch of garlic powder. Be sure to pat seafood dry before dipping, then fry as usual. Great for veggies and mushrooms too. Make the batter a little thicker for chicken and steak fingers and experiment with seasonings to your taste.

Made a batch for my family and I, it was a real hit especially since I had substituted the beer with ginger ale instead, which gave it a nice ginger taste to them. I had also added a few other spices to the batter itself to give it more flavor.
I would make these again, since they're much lighter then normal onion rings.

Excellent base recipe! I also dredged the onion rings in flour before dipping them in the batter-- great idea to help the batter stick. Definitely need to add salt, and some spices if you're up for it. I used 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp seasoning salt, and 1 tsp cajun seasoning and some freshly ground black pepper. We still had to salt them after frying them, an easy problem to fix next time. This batch was enough for one large onion. I pan-fried these in about two cups of canola oil, had to flip some of the large ones once. We dipped these in the sauce from allrecipe's Blooming Onion and Dipping Sauce. What a special treat for our family! And we didn't have to step foot into a certain steakhouse!

This recipe was GREAT! I made a few small changes. I used O'Doul's instead of real beer, I added about 1 1/2 t. Old Bay Seasoning along with the salt and pepper. And last, but not least, after coating the onion rings with the batter, I dipped them in panko bread crumbs. WOW!! Extra crunchy and beautiful golden brown! Left my camera at work, so took a pic with my phone but can't figure out how to send it to the computer from the phone. Will post a pic as soon as I get that taken care of. :-) Thanks for sharing this recipe...it is wonderful!

I am only giving this a 4 because if I hadn't read the reviews and followed some of the other reviews, they wouldn't have turned out. With the changes I would give this a 5. I added garlic powder, seasoning salt, paprika to the flour mixture. I had to use a lot more than 1 cup of beer so the batter wasn't quite as thick. I dredged the onions in flour first which helped with the batter staying on the onions. I didn't even have enough batter to coat 3 onions and they weren't that large. If you followed this to a tee, I think they would be pretty bland. I will make them again and just double the flour mixture.
My FaVoRiTe recipe by far...have tried 5 or 6..even with panko..and I love these. I added garlic powder and let sit for about 10minutes with the beer! A little messy but well worth it

This batter was so easy! I fried the onion rings and some zucchini medallions in the deep fryer. The batter turned out crispy and light. For seasoning I used garlic salt and black pepper. Dipped the fried zucchini in some warm spaghetti sauce topped with mozzarella. Just like the ones you get in a pub. Delicious. Thank you for sharing!
Excellent. I added more beer than the recipe calls for, as my batter was too thick.
Foolproof! Crispy, crunchy-just as good as a restaurant, maybe better!
Love love love this recipe. Crisp, not too thick and for minimal ingredients the taste is great!

Followed recipe exactly and made excellent onion rings on my first ever attempt! The batter stayed on the rings perfectly resulting is a crisp yet not too thick coating. Onions were still soft and juicy underneath. Used 1015 onions that a friend brought from Texas. Thanks!

My favorite batter. I do have to say I think I will cut the rings thicker next time so I won't have to cook so many, and because I like the onion to be just a little firm when lightly browned. I did notice that the batter seemed to continue to cook (and get darker) after I took them out so I will take them out of the oil just as soon as they start to turn a little golden.

Superb! wanted something fried and I'm vegetarian..only veggie I had in stock that would work. So easy that my husband did it and said he could make these everyday. I forgot the black pepper but it was still devine...Very crunchy. No more buying onion rings. Way better than your favorite restaurant ones too
Great recipe! But next time will add more seasoning, I think they lack flavor a bit with just the pinch of salt and pepper.
Very very bland! Also, 4 onions are way to much for the batter. I used about 1 1/2 onions and the batter was gone.
This recipe is awesome. Tastes just like a good restaurant quality onion rings. Simple recipe too. I like batter onion rings better than the breaded kind.
